description: March 6 birthday meaning: Pisces decan 2, birthday number 6, Life Path by year, Chinese zodiac note and famous birthdays.
answer: In Western astrology, a March 6 birthday falls in Pisces, in the second decan, with Neptune as the sign's ruler and Moon as the decan's. In numerology the day gives birthday number 6. The Life Path also uses the birth year. Pisces is mutable and water.

sections.heading: March 6 zodiac sign and personality
paragraphs: On March 6, Pisces sits around its midpoint, fifteen degrees in, under the Moon's sub-rulership. Six is numerology's nurturing number, so the date is commonly read as one of the zodiac's most caring: a person who parents the whole group, remembers birthdays and treats the comfort of others as a serious responsibility.

On March 6 the Sun usually sits at about 15° Pisces, in the second decan, where Moon is the sub-ruler alongside Neptune. The Moon, which rules Cancer, acts as sub-ruler for Pisces between 10 and 19 degrees, roughly the first ten days of March. This decan tends to turn the sign's compassion towards home, family and the people closest at hand. Early-March birthdays are often linked with nurturing, intuitive and emotionally receptive temperaments, with long memories and a deep need to feel safe. The lunar influence can make moods ebb and flow in quick cycles. When they look after their own emotional tides as carefully as they tend other people's, these Pisceans often become the steady harbour that others return to.

sections.heading: March 6 in numerology
paragraphs: A birthday on the 6th produces a birthday number of 6, unreduced. As the secondary number in a chart, the day of birth hints at how someone naturally contributes to the people around them. The 6 is the number of the household in Pythagorean tradition: care, responsibility, beauty in the home and fairness within the family. Those born on the 6th are often the friend who remembers birthdays and notices when someone is struggling. Their usual lesson is that looking after others works best when they include themselves in the circle of care too.

The Life Path, the main number in a numerology chart, also uses the birth year, so it changes from one March 6 birthday to the next: it is 7 for 1960, 8 for 1970, 9 for 1980 and 1 for 1990, for example. Some birth years on this date reach the master number 11.

sections.heading: Born on March 6: season, famous birthdays and Chinese zodiac
paragraphs: A March birthday falls around the spring equinox for the northern hemisphere, the season of thaw and first growth, while southern birthdays mark the turn into autumn. The month is split between Pisces and Aries, with the change around March 20 or 21. In numerology March is month 3, linked with expression, creativity and sociability, a lively number for a month that ends with the zodiac starting over. March 6 is the 65th day of the year (66th in a leap year). By March 21, 15 days later, the Sun has usually moved on into Aries.

For the Chinese zodiac, Lunar New Year has always passed by March 6, so the animal is simply the one for the birth year. Well-known people born on March 6 include Gabriel García Márquez (1927), Valentina Tereshkova (1937) and Elizabeth Barrett Browning (1806).

faq.question: What zodiac sign is March 6?
faq.answer: March 6 is Pisces in every year from 1930 to 2030, wherever you were born. It falls in the second decan of Pisces, which tradition links with Moon.

faq.question: What is the Life Path number for someone born on March 6?
faq.answer: It depends on the birth year. On March 6 the Life Path is 7 in 1960, 8 in 1970, 9 in 1980, 1 in 1990, 11 in 2000, 3 in 2010 and 4 in 2020. The birthday number, from the day alone, is 6 for everyone born on the 6th.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac sign is someone born on March 6?
faq.answer: Chinese astrology is straightforward for a March 6 birthday: the new year began weeks earlier, so the birth year's own animal applies.

faq.question: Which famous people were born on March 6?
faq.answer: March 6 is also the birthday of Gabriel García Márquez (1927), Valentina Tereshkova (1937) and Elizabeth Barrett Browning (1806). The list comes from Wikidata and favours people with the most Wikipedia articles.
